resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. strategy_tie_in §4 (mood-doesn't-resolve-early facet; teaching moment lands) line 11: scope: Refuted on rule fit. I read §4 with rule.js and in check_strategy_tie_in.md. It is the "Strategy-fidelity check": before designing or reviewing a module, pull per-module sequencing claims from the content-strategy doc and verify the draft doesn't front-run a DOWNSTREAM module's teaching moment. It is about cross-module sequencing. It has no "mood-doesn't-resolve-early" facet and nothing about a piece answering its own take-home. The mood text is §1, which concerns module mood stewing into the NEXT module's moment, and it is not what the judge cited.

The facts the judge counted are accurate. L7 says "no step in the workflow opened the source", L11 says "Nobody checked a legal research database", and slide bullet 4 (slides/why-the-llm-fabricates.md) says "has no step where someone opens the cited source". L41 is the take-home. But none of this front-runs a later module. In content-strategy.md (Grounded Output) M5's mood is "Rescue" ("Ahh, this is actually fixable"), and its teaching moment is the four-detector benchmark and saved judge. The prework is M5's own arming reading. The strategy says both cases "have the organisational missing-check on public record" and that the student arrives with one sentence per case. It also says the prework seeds M5's classification and Technique 1, so the check is meant to be learnable from the cases. Nothing here steals M3/M4 unease or M6's leverage.

The "newly rewritten, reveal not authorised" framing is mostly wrong. Commit 12fbd424 (2026-08-03) is what removed the bold "The missing check:" reveals and wrote the L49 note. It deliberately left the factual sentence "He did not check the cases in a legal research database", and the PASS audits were stamped on that text. Nov's ef356fd4 is a commit with "maintainer yes 2026-11-06" that re-aimed M5 toward grounding, and it kept the same fact in L11 ("Nobody checked a legal research database"). The only truly new sentence is L7's generalisation. The maintainer-approved prior state therefore already tolerated naming the Mata fact. L49's actual prohibition is the bold reveals, and those are not restored.

The BLOCKING severity does not hold under the cited rule. The most that survives is a possible tension between L49's wording ("unnamed in both case sections") and L7 or the slide bullet. That is a maintainer-note or pedagogy matter, not a §4 BLOCK. It is a note-versus-body drift to reconcile, not a defect in a body that was correct. / harm: The finding fails on three grounds. It is built on a misreading of the rule. The fix would not remove the reveal it claims to remove. The reveal-bearing sentence existed when the maintainer note was written, and that note was written to allow it.

**1. Wrong rule.** check_strategy_tie_in.md §4 is the strategy-fidelity check. It asks whether a draft front-runs a downstream module's teaching moment (a cross-module sequencing claim). The mood-resolution rule is §1. This prework belongs to M5, and its take-home seeds M5's own Phase 2. It does not front-run any later module. The finding grants §4 but files a different rule's harm under it.

**2. The fix is a no-op, because other lines carry the same meaning.**
- L5, which the judge leaves alone, says "which **organisational check was missing**".
- L13, also left alone, says "The order blames the missing verification, not the tool." That names the answer ("verification") outright. Cutting L7 and L11 leaves the check named in L5 and L13.
- The slide `why-the-llm-fabricates.md` says "Verification has to leave the session and touch the source." Bullet 4 says "no step where someone opens the cited source". That slide is a separate file, and the proposed fix does not touch it.
- L41's task asks for a sentence in the student's own words. Removing L11 does not stop a student writing "verification before submission", because L13 already hands that over.

**3. L11 restates a fact that was already there when the maintainer note was written.**
- `git blame` shows the L49 note dates from 2026-08-03 (commit 12fbd424).
- The pre-rewrite body, visible in the ef356fd4 diff, already read "He did not check the cases in a legal research database." That is the same fact as L11.
- That body also said "The verification step still wasn't built in. What that step would have been is the sentence you bring to class."
- The note's wording is "Do not restore the bold 'The missing check:' reveals". It bans the labelled bold answer-lines. It does not ban stating that no one checked a database, which is a case fact and is the Mata story itself.
- ef356fd4 actually shortened the reveal. The old body explicitly gave "the missing verification, not ChatGPT" and "gatekeeping duty". The new body says less.

**4. Fixing it costs more than the defect.** L11's "Nobody checked a legal research database" is the factual hinge of the Mata story: ChatGPT said yes, and no one went outside the session. Cutting it weakens the case summary. The student is still supposed to read the Justia order, where the missing check is documented.

**5. Counts and facts.** I verified the three quoted spans (L7, L11, slide bullet 4). The L41 task text and L49 maintainer note are as quoted. Commits ef356fd4 and 76528a6c exist and touched the file or slide. The judge's counts hold, but they do not support the conclusion.

**Harm lens.** No student in the room is worse off. The take-home is still "name X in your own words". Any reveal that exists comes from L5 and L13, which the fix does not touch. The only live issue is a possible stale-note wording mismatch, which is a note tidy-up and not a BLOCK.
